review_basis:
navfac-cherry-point-atc-mechanical.pdf#18 (MP101) is the second navfac coordinator pick named in reports/LINEAR_HELDOUT.txt, and that file's own text records it as ATTEMPTED, NOT AUTHORED: one earlier seed near a real '2"ø HHWR' label ran away to 11,809 LF across a fully-looped hydronic network (not a fair single-call target), and a second seed's own dead_end calls looked premature against a duct line that visibly continued past both marked stops. Neither was trustworthy, so the sheet was set aside rather than forced.

Revisiting it this pass, the first text-anchor scan (the same combined `\d+"?\s*(SYS)` pattern used successfully elsewhere in this corpus) found only 2 hits across this sheet's own 390 text spans -- implausibly few for a sheet this dense (61,641 segments at cold build). The cause: this sheet formats many of its own real size+system callouts as e.g. '1 1/2"ø HHWS' and '2"ø CHWR', with a literal ø (diameter symbol) glyph sitting between the inch mark and the system token -- a format the strict regex never accounted for. A broader, ø-aware scan without that combined-token constraint surfaced many more real candidates that the first pass had silently missed.

Four candidates from that broader sweep were tried and rejected before this one, each a previously-established rejection pathology, not a new failure mode: (1) seeds near a '1 1/2"ø HHWR' label at [2739.1,1432.8] repeatedly produced ~401 LF traces with cap/cap stops and 134 vertices -- the corpus's own recognized hatching-mistrace signature (a dense hatched area read as one long run), not real pipe ink; (2) a seed at [2739.1,1372.8] produced a 4 LF, round:2, CHWR trace (dead_end/dead_end at [2740.1,1362.7] and [2812.1,1362.7]) that a marked crop confirmed sits exactly on a label's own tiny leader-dot/tick-mark artifact, not drawn pipe; (3) and (4) seeds near stacked '2.5"ø CHWS'/'2.5"ø CHWR' labels at [1961.5,1792.8] and [1966.8,1824] both produced ~44.8 LF traces with systems read backwards from their own seed label (CHWS seed reading CHWR, and vice versa) and ambiguous/ambiguous stops -- the corpus's own recognized system-crosstalk pattern between two closely-parallel real pipes, genuinely undecidable at this zoom, not a safe golden.

The candidate actually used (seed [2741.2,1779.2], 12.53 LF, round:2 CHWR, dead_end/dead_end) was confirmed through both a wide marked crop and two very tight per-endpoint crops (session.viewSheet at 15x zoom, ring marks at each raw endpoint): the traced span is the LOWER of two closely-parallel horizontal double-stroke pipe lines. A tight zoom at the label leader junction shows two separate arrowheads terminating at two different heights on these two distinct strokes -- the upper arrowhead (from a '2"ø CHWS' label) lands on the UPPER stroke, and the lower arrowhead (from a '2"ø CHWR' label) lands on the SAME LOWER stroke the trace's own two rings sit on -- confirming the automatic 'beside' CHWR/round:2 bind against a real, visually distinguishable sibling line, not the crosstalk pattern rejected above. The two dead_end stops are each a genuine drawn feature, not narrative or arbitrary cuts: the backward (west) stop at [2689.9,1777.9] sits exactly where this horizontal run crosses a real, much-thicker vertical riser pipe (a genuine T/cross junction, confirmed at 15x zoom -- the horizontal line's own segment continuity breaks against the wider perpendicular stroke, not against empty space); the forward (east) stop at [2915.5,1777.9] sits exactly where the same stroke caps against a real dashed vertical partition/wall line bordering room 136 (KITCHEN/BREAK, visible in the wider crop) -- the pipe's own ink genuinely ends there, it does not fade out or run off-render. A reseed from the exact same seed coordinate against the freshly re-loaded, already-committed raw PDF reproduced the identical points, length, size, and system read.
scope: The second and final navfac coordinator pick named in reports/LINEAR_HELDOUT.txt's frozen split (the sibling pick, navfac-cherry-point-atc-mechanical.pdf#6/MH101, is already authored as ground_truth/linear/navfac-mh101-heldout.json). This run is a single 2" round CHWR (chilled water return) pipe segment (12.53 LF) on a dense mechanical piping plan, from a real T-junction against a vertical riser main to a real cap at a wall/partition line near room 136. Explicitly OUT OF SCOPE: the four rejected candidates described in review_basis (a hatching-mistrace loop, a leader-artifact mistrace, and two CHWS/CHWR system-crosstalk ambiguous-stop pairs -- none usable as ground truth); the parallel 2" CHWS line running directly beside this run; the vertical riser main this run T's into; the '1 1/2"ø HHWS/R' and '3/4"ø CHWS/R' up-riser callouts referenced on this same sheet ('...UP TO FLOOR ABOVE. SEE MP104 FOR CONTINUATION' -- a different sheet, out of this corpus's scope entirely); every other duct and pipe run on this same dense sheet; bldg5406-hvac-demo-mechanical.pdf#2 (M-101), the one remaining held-out sheet in this file's own frozen list that stays permanently unauthored (confirmed exhausted).
